summary: Players know nine of the ten languages, but the order is Wikipedia's quirk: Cebuano #2 and Swedish #5 are mostly bot-written, while Chinese, Japanese, Arabic and Portuguese just miss. A casual player finds 6, at the hard end of the target, and the reveal is the best part.
reasons: Casual (the world's big languages, in the order they come to mind) found 6 and lost all 5 lives on Chinese #12, Japanese #13, Arabic #15, Hindi #62 and Korean #23. The order swings it: 5 with the Asian languages first, 9 for a player who reads the first two misses and turns to Europe (Dutch, Swedish, Polish). A crowd average near 5 is the floor of the target, where painters sat when a player called it too hard.

Cebuano delights more than it frustrates. Nobody types it, so it costs no life; it is the one stretch answer, and its reveal (6.1 million articles, nearly all from Lsjbot, 197 active users) is the best moment on the list. The frustration comes from the famous misses landing in a row, but four of them are close (#12 to #18) and each shows its count, so the lesson lands.

The prompt says plainly what is counted (a language's Wikipedia, by articles). The top 10 matches the source table, every fact is quoted, and the merged editions keep the larger count and stay free (Bokmal 695,503; Kurmanji 92,409; official Belarusian 275,737). 'wikipedia', 'language', 'china' and 'sweden' hand over nothing; 'arabic' is Arabic #15, not Egyptian Arabic #11.

Fan found 10, losing lives on Japanese, Chinese and Portuguese. As a Blitz it is deep (25 of 26 scored) but plays much like the existing Most spoken languages Blitz. That list differs enough as a classic (only English, Spanish and French overlap), but another language list, languages-countries, is also a debut: keep them in different weeks.
fixes: 'bisaya' (what most Cebuano speakers call their language, per the Cebuano language article) is offered as Bislama (#293), a life if confirmed; 'binisaya' reads as no answer. Add 'Bisaya' and 'Binisaya' as aliases of Cebuano, with a guard in aliases.test.ts ('bisaya' -> correct Cebuano).

'sorani' is still offered as Somali (#159). Its knownNames entry only takes effect after the lexicon retrain in docs/REBUILD_QUEUE.md, which must land before this runs; add 'sorani' -> unknown to the wikipedia-languages guards.

Fair names that read as no answer (free, but no rank shown and no Blitz score): add 'Farsi' to Persian (#19), 'Hokkien' to Southern Min (#36), 'Filipino' to Tagalog (#107), and 'Castilian' and 'Espanol' to Spanish (the 'Castilian language' alias doesn't reach the bare word).
'flemish' is offered only as West Flemish (#186); Flemish usually means Belgian Dutch. Add 'Flemish' to Dutch as well, so the game offers both.
